title: Measuring Length: Millimetres, Centimetres, Metres and Kilometres
seo_title: Millimetres, Centimetres, Metres and Kilometres Class 4 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 6)
standard_code: Class 4, Maths Mela Chapter 6: Measuring Length
standard_text: Measurement of length: estimating and measuring in mm, cm, m and km, converting between units, and solving problems (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 4)
meta_desc: Class 4 Measuring Length worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 6): mm, cm, m and km, reading scales, converting and problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Choose the unit to suit the length.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 10 mm = 1 cm; 100 cm = 1 m; 1,000 m = 1 km.
  • A pencil is measured in cm, a room in m, a journey in km.

Examples

Example

Write 3 m 25 cm in cm.

3 × 100 + 25

Answer: 325 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using 10 cm = 1 m100 cm make 1 m.
Measuring from 1 on the rulerStart at 0.

faq.q: How many metres are in a kilometre?

faq.a: A tenth of a centimetre; the tiny marks on a ruler.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much water a bathtub holds?
items.e: A bathtub holds a lot of water, about 150 L. Use litres. Grams and kilograms measure mass, not capacity.

items.q: Which tool is best for measuring the length of a pencil?
items.e: A pencil is short, so a ruler marked in centimetres and millimetres is best.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a bag of potatoes?
items.e: A bag of potatoes is heavy to carry. Heavy things are measured in kilograms. Millilitres and litres measure capacity, not mass.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much medicine fits on a spoon?
items.e: A spoon holds only about 5 mL. Use millilitres. Grams and kilograms measure mass, not capacity.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much a juice box holds?
items.e: A juice box holds only about 200 mL. Small amounts are measured in millilitres. Grams and kilograms measure mass, not capacity.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the width of a maths book?
items.e: A book is about 21 cm wide. Use centimetres.

items.q: Which tool is best for measuring the distance around your head?
items.e: A measuring tape bends, so it can go around a curved shape. A ruler is stiff and cannot bend.

items.q: Which tool is best for measuring the mass of an apple?
items.e: Mass is measured with a scale or a pan balance. A measuring cup measures capacity.

items.q: Which tool is best for measuring 250 mL of milk for a recipe?
items.e: Capacity is measured with a measuring cup or a measuring jug. A scale measures mass.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a crayon?
items.e: A crayon fits in your hand and is about 9 cm long. Use centimetres.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a hockey rink?
items.e: A hockey rink is about 60 m long. Long lengths you can walk are measured in metres.

items.q: Which tool is best for measuring the length of the school hallway?
items.e: A trundle wheel clicks every metre as you roll it, so it is good for long lengths. A 30 cm ruler is much too short.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of an ant?
items.e: An ant is tiny, only a few millimetres long. Use the smallest unit, millimetres.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the height of a classroom door?
items.e: A door is a bit taller than a grown-up, about 2 m. 20 m is as tall as a 6-storey building.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1 kg 500 g = 1,500 g and 1 kg 50 g = 1,050 g. 1,500 g is the most. Do not compare only the numbers 1 and 1,450.

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 1 m 20 cm = 120 cm and 1 m 5 cm = 105 cm. 150 cm is the longest.

items.q: Which holds the most?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 1 L 250 mL = 1,250 mL and 1 L 50 mL = 1,050 mL. 1,500 mL is the most.
Each mark is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. A shows 2 kg 750 g and B shows 3 kg 250 g. B is heavier. From 2 kg 750 g to 3 kg is 250 g, and to 3 kg 250 g is 250 g more: 500 g.

items.q: Which list goes from the coldest to the warmest?
items.e: Below zero is colder than 0 °C. −2 °C is the coldest, then 0 °C, then 3 °C.

items.q: At the swimming carnival, Gauri’s stopwatch shows 00:58. Varun’s stopwatch shows 01:02. Who is faster, and by how much?
items.e: 00:58 is 58 s. 01:02 is 1 min 2 s = 62 s. The smaller time is faster, so Gauri wins. 62 − 58 = 4 s.

items.q: On a ruler, how many small spaces are there from 3 cm to 4 cm?
items.e: There are 9 small marks between 3 and 4, but 10 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks. Each space is 1 mm, and 10 mm = 1 cm.
It starts at 0. It ends 7 small spaces past 4 cm. Each small space is 1 mm, so it is 4 cm 7 mm = 47 mm.
It starts at 0. It ends 2 small spaces past 6 cm. Each small space is 1 mm, so it is 6 cm 2 mm = 62 mm.
It starts at 0. It ends 5 small spaces past 8 cm. Each small space is 1 mm, so it is 8 cm 5 mm = 85 mm.
It does not start at 0. It starts at 20 mm and ends at 58 mm. 58 − 20 = 38 mm, which is 3 cm 8 mm.
It does not start at 0. It starts at 30 mm and ends at 74 mm. 74 − 30 = 44 mm, which is 4 cm 4 mm.
It does not start at 0. It starts at 15 mm and ends at 52 mm. 52 − 15 = 37 mm, which is 3 cm 7 mm.
It does not start at 0. It starts at 40 mm and ends at 96 mm. 96 − 40 = 56 mm, which is 5 cm 6 mm.
It does not start at 0. It starts at 25 mm and ends at 70 mm. 70 − 25 = 45 mm, which is 4 cm 5 mm.

items.q: What does the tape measure show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 cm ÷ 10 = 1 cm. Count the spaces after 140 cm: 141 cm, 142 cm, 143 cm. So it is 143 cm.

items.q: What does the tape measure show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 cm. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 cm ÷ 5 = 2 cm. Count the spaces after 120 cm: 122 cm, 124 cm, 126 cm. So it is 126 cm.

items.q: What does the tape measure show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 cm. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 cm ÷ 5 = 2 cm. Count the spaces after 80 cm: 82 cm, 84 cm. So it is 84 cm.

items.q: What does the tape measure show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 50 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 50 cm ÷ 10 = 5 cm. Count the spaces after 200 cm: 205 cm, 210 cm, 215 cm, 220 cm, 225 cm, 230 cm, 235 cm. So it is 235 cm.

items.q: What does the tape measure show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 50 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 50 cm ÷ 10 = 5 cm. Count the spaces after 150 cm: 155 cm, 160 cm, 165 cm. So it is 165 cm.
The numbers go up by 10 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 cm ÷ 10 = 1 cm. Count the spaces after 30 cm: 31 cm, 32 cm, 33 cm, 34 cm, 35 cm, 36 cm, 37 cm. So it is 37 cm.

items.q: A long tape measure is used at the athletics carnival. What does it show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 1 m = 100 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 10 = 10 cm, not 1 cm. The pointer is 3 marks past 2 m: 2 m 30 cm.

items.q: A long tape measure is used at the athletics carnival. What does it show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 1 m = 100 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 10 = 10 cm, not 1 cm. The pointer is 7 marks past 1 m: 1 m 70 cm.

items.q: A ruler is broken, so it starts at 4 cm. A feather goes from the 4 cm mark to the 13 cm mark. How long is the feather?
items.e: It does not start at 0, so take the start away from the end: 13 − 4 = 9 cm.

items.q: A tape measure has the numbers 10, 20, 30, … and 5 spaces between each pair of numbers. What is each mark worth?
items.e: From one number to the next is 10 cm. 10 cm shared into 5 spaces: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 cm.

items.q: Each small mark on a tape measure is worth 5 cm. A line ends 3 marks past 40 cm. Where does it end?
items.e: Count on 3 marks of 5 cm from 40: 45, 50, 55. It ends at 55 cm.

items.q: How many millimetres are in 1 centimetre?
items.e: Look at a ruler: there are 10 small marks in each centimetre. 1 cm = 10 mm.

items.q: How many centimetres are in 1 metre?
items.e: Centi means one hundredth, so 1 m = 100 cm. A metre stick has 100 cm marked on it.

items.q: How many metres are in 1 kilometre?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000, so 1 km = 1,000 m (not 100 m).

items.q: About how thick is a ₹1 coin?
items.e: A ₹1 coin is very thin, about 3 millimetres. 3 cm is even more than the width of the whole coin.

items.q: About how tall is a classroom door?
items.e: A door is a little taller than a grown-up, about 2 metres. 2 cm is shorter than your finger.

items.q: Students walk for about 15 minutes. About how far do they go?
items.e: In 15 minutes you can walk about 1 kilometre (1,000 m). 1 m is just one big step.

items.q: Convert. 6 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so you need more millimetres: multiply. 6 × 10 = 60, so 6 cm = 60 mm.

items.q: Convert. 7 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so you need more centimetres: multiply. 7 × 100 = 700, so 7 m = 700 cm.

items.q: Convert. 4 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so you need more metres: multiply. 4 × 1,000 = 4,000, so 4 km = 4,000 m.

items.q: Convert. 90 mm = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so you need fewer centimetres: divide. 90 ÷ 10 = 9, so 90 mm = 9 cm.

items.q: Convert. 800 cm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so you need fewer metres: divide. 800 ÷ 100 = 8, so 800 cm = 8 m.

items.q: Convert. 9,000 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so you need fewer kilometres: divide. 9,000 ÷ 1,000 = 9, so 9,000 m = 9 km.

items.q: Convert. 12 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so you need more metres: multiply. 12 × 1,000 = 12,000, so 12 km = 12,000 m.
The pencil ends 4 small marks after 6 cm, so it is 6 cm 4 mm long. 1 cm = 10 mm, so 6 × 10 = 60, and 60 + 4 = 64 mm.
The pencil reaches 5 whole centimetres and then 7 small marks. Each small mark is 1 mm, so it is 5 cm 7 mm long (57 mm).
The pencil starts at 1 cm, not at 0. It ends at 8 cm 3 mm = 83 mm. Take away the start: 83 − 10 = 73 mm.

items.q: Convert. 3 m 5 cm = ☐ cm
items.e: 3 m = 300 cm. Add the 5 cm: 300 + 5 = 305 cm. Writing 35 cm forgets that 3 m is 300 cm.

items.q: Convert. 2 km 30 m = ☐ m
items.e: 2 km = 2,000 m. Add the 30 m: 2,000 + 30 = 2,030 m. The 3 goes in the tens place, not the hundreds.

items.q: Which is the same as 450 cm?
items.e: 100 cm = 1 m, so 400 cm = 4 m. 450 cm = 4 m and 50 cm left over.

items.q: Which is the same as 5,600 m?
items.e: 1,000 m = 1 km, so 5,000 m = 5 km. 5,600 m = 5 km and 600 m left over.

items.q: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, so 1,000 millilitres make 1 litre: 1 L = 1,000 mL.

items.q: Which unit is one thousandth of a litre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, and litres measure capacity. So a millilitre is one thousandth of a litre.

items.q: Which unit is one hundredth of a metre?
items.e: Centi means one hundredth, so a centimetre is one hundredth of a metre. A millimetre is one thousandth of a metre.

items.q: The ribbon is 1 cm long. How many millimetres is that?
items.e: Count the small spaces from 0 to 1: there are 10. Each small space is 1 mm, so 1 cm = 10 mm.

items.q: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000, so 1 kg = 1,000 g. Watch out: 1 kg is not 100 g.

items.q: In kilometre and kilogram, what does kilo mean?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000. 1 kilometre = 1,000 metres and 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams.

items.q: Which unit is 1,000 times as long as a metre?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000, so a kilometre is 1,000 metres. A kilogram is 1,000 grams: it measures mass, not length.

items.q: In millilitre and millimetre, what does milli mean?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth. A millilitre is one thousandth of a litre, so 1,000 mL = 1 L.

items.q: How many millimetres are in 1 metre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, so 1 m = 1,000 mm. (Check: 1 m = 100 cm and each cm is 10 mm: 100 × 10 = 1,000.)

items.q: Order the units from shortest to longest.
items.e: A millimetre is the tiniest. 10 mm make 1 cm, 100 cm make 1 m, and 1,000 m make 1 km.

items.q: Which length is the greatest?
items.e: Change to metres: 1 km = 1,000 m, 999 cm is less than 10 m, and 5,000 mm = 5 m. 1 km is the greatest even though 1 is the smallest number.

items.q: Which capacity is the least?
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL and 2 L = 2,000 mL. 950 mL is less than 1,000 mL, 1,200 mL and 2,000 mL.

items.q: 3 km = ☐ m
5 m = ☐ cm
7 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm, so 7 cm = 7 × 10 = 70 mm.

items.q: A bigger unit gives a smaller number. Which is true?
items.e: Metres are bigger than centimetres, so you need more centimetres: 4 × 100 = 400. 4 m = 400 cm.

items.q: How many metres are in 12 km?
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Half of 1,000 is 500, so 12 km = 500 m. 50 m would mean 1 km = 100 m.

items.q: How many grams are in 14 kg?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. To find a quarter, divide by 4: 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g.

items.q: How many millilitres are in 34 l?
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. One quarter is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL, so three quarters is 3 × 250 = 750 mL.

items.q: Convert. 1.5 L = ☐ ml
Lakshmi walks 1 km 200 m to school in the morning. She walks the same way home after school. How far does she walk altogether?
Yash is baking a cake. The recipe needs 350 g of flour. He has a 1 kg bag of flour. How much flour is left after baking?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Subtract: 1,000 − 350 = 650 g. Take care when you exchange: the answer is not 750 g.

items.q: A film is 130 minutes long. How long is it in hours and minutes?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 2 hours = 120 minutes. 130 − 120 = 10, so it is 2 hours 10 minutes. 1 hour 30 minutes would mean 1 hour = 100 minutes.

items.q: Nisha swims 50 lengths of a 25 m pool in a sponsored swim. How far does she swim?
A sponsored walk is 5 km long. It has 4 equal stages. How long is each stage in metres?
items.e: 5 km = 5,000 m. Share it into 4 equal parts: 5,000 ÷ 4 = 1,250 m.

items.q: A bottle holds 2 litres of squash. Six cups of 250 mL are poured from it. How much squash is left?
Neha is 8 years 7 months old. How old is she in months?
items.e: 1 year = 12 months, so 8 years = 8 × 12 = 96 months. Add the 7 months: 96 + 7 = 103 months.

items.q: The summer holiday is 6 weeks long. How many days is that?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 6 × 7 = 42 days.

items.q: In PE, Kabir holds a plank for 2 minutes 15 seconds. How many seconds is that?
items.e: 2 minutes = 2 × 60 = 120 seconds. Add 15: 120 + 15 = 135 seconds.

items.q: In the Multiplication Tables Check there are 25 questions. Students get 6 seconds for each one. How long is that altogether?
items.e: 25 × 6 = 150 seconds. 120 seconds = 2 minutes, and 150 − 120 = 30, so it is 2 minutes 30 seconds.

items.q: What mass does the scale show?
items.e: The numbers are kilograms, and 1 kg = 1,000 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 2 kg + 750 g = 2 kg 750 g.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers are litres, and 1 L = 1,000 mL. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The top of the water is 1 line above 1 L: 1 L 250 mL.
The numbers are kilograms, and 1 kg = 1,000 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 5 = 200 g. The needle is 2 marks past 1 kg: 1 kg + 400 g = 1 kg 400 g.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers are litres, and 1 L = 1,000 mL. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 2 = 500 mL. The top of the water is 1 line above 2 L: 2 L 500 mL.
The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 g. The needle is 3 marks past 400: 400 + 150 = 550 g.

items.q: What mass does the scale show?
items.e: The numbers are kilograms, and 1 kg = 1,000 g. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 2 = 500 g. The needle is 1 mark past 3 kg: 3 kg + 500 g = 3 kg 500 g.

items.q: The scale shows Kavya’s backpack. She takes out a 600 g lunch. What is the mass of the backpack now?
items.e: Each mark is 500 g, so the scale shows 3 kg 500 g = 3,500 g. Taking out the lunch makes it lighter: 3,500 − 600 = 2,900 g.

items.q: Meera wants 2 L of water in the jug for the plants. How much more water does she need?
items.e: Each line is 250 mL, so the jug has 1 L 250 mL = 1,250 mL. 2 L = 2,000 mL. 2,000 − 1,250 = 750 mL more.

items.q: A bag of milk holds 4 L. How many millilitres is that?
Imran’s hockey bag has a mass of 9 kg. He adds his skates, which have a mass of 1 kg 500 g. What is the mass of the bag now?
items.e: Add the kilograms: 9 + 1 = 10 kg. Then add the 500 g: 10 kg 500 g.
